full_article:
The idea

The research explored how people affected by disasters can have a stronger voice in decisions about recovery and rebuilding. Focusing on Nepal, the study looked at how communities, civil society activists and campaign groups responded to the 2015 earthquakes, the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2024 floods. Dr Dhungana has developed a longer-term research relationship to examine the barriers that prevent local people from influencing recovery efforts and has explored ways to improve accountability, participation and fairness in post-disaster recovery and reconstruction. The thinking behind this? These policies and programmes will be more effective and equitable when approached from a rights-based perspective and shaped by the people most affected by them.

A Rapido driver, a labourer, and a minor are among the accused who opened fire at Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff's car as the actor was leaving a football club in Mumbai's Juhu area on Sunday night, police said. The accused were intercepted in Rajasthan's Kota, while they were on a train and headed to Delhi, police said, adding, they wanted to flee to Nepal.

The three accused received Rs 50,000 collectively as advance to carry out the attack, according to police sources. Investigators are questioning the accused to establish their individual roles and determine whether all three were directly involved in the shooting.

The 36-year-old actor, wearing a muscle tee and seated in the front, was waving at his fans through the rolled up car windows, when the shots rang out. A man in front, holding up a gun supported by both hands, fired at the car, showed a video. Another man, wearing a cap, was seen firing from the side. A man on a bike was stationed right there and the three then fled on it, the video showed.

full_article:
Kathmandu, Oct 19: The Armed Police Force Nepal has been providing free transport service to facilitate the movement of the general people within Kathmandu Valley on the occasion of Dashain.

The APF Nepal has operated two buses for three days from today for this purpose. Assistant Spokesperson of the APF Nepal, Shailendra Thapa, shared that free bus service has been operated with the aim of facilitating the citizens in their movement as the public transport in the Kathmandu Valley is very limited during Dashain festival.

These buses would provide service from 8:00 am to 6:00 pm in various routes. A bus departing from APF Nepal Headquarters in Halchowk would provide service to passengers of Balaju, New Bus Park, Koteshwor, Sardobato, Balkhu.

Similarly, passengers of Sitapaila, Kalanki, Koteshwor, New Bus Park as well as other places would be benefitted from another bus departing from Halchowk. (RSS)

full_article:
JioHotstar has expanded to Nepal through a partnership with DGO, following its recent launches in the Middle East and North Africa, and earlier launches in the UK, Canada and Singapore.

Under the partnership, DGO will offer a dedicated JioHotstar section featuring films, originals, television shows, reality content and kids’ programming.

The launch catalogue includes films such as Bhediya, 12th Fail, Kesari Chapter 2, Super 30 and Welcome to the Jungle. JioHotstar Originals available in Nepal include Hunkkaar, Pritam & Pedro, Ali Baba Aur 40 Bhoot, Special Ops and Chiraiya.

The offering also includes titles such as Bigg Boss, Koffee with Karan and India Ka Top 1 Percent, along with selected regional content available in Hindi.

JioHotstar will be available through DGO’s Mobile and Plus plans, with launch pricing starting at NPR 249 per month. The service can be accessed through DGO’s website and app across iOS, Android, Android TV and Smart TV.

DGO’s existing catalogue of Nepali films and shows will sit alongside the JioHotstar offering, with the platform adding a new Nepali film every week. Subscribers will also have access to live international sports, including LaLiga, MotoGP and the Carabao Cup.

Amit Malhotra, head- International Business, JioStar, said: “JioHotstar’s international expansion is bringing together the scale of what we have created in India and the demand for Indian entertainment overseas. Nepal is an important part of that journey, with audiences who have followed our films, television shows and talent for generations. With DGO, we can give that audience a much broader offering, combining JioHotstar’s entertainment with the convenience of a local platform. We see considerable scope in Nepal to build on this existing relationship and make JioHotstar part of everyday viewing across households.”

Roshan Niraula, chief executive officer- DGO, said: “This partnership is a milestone for DGO and for Nepal’s entertainment industry. Our ambition is to give Nepali viewers more reasons to choose DGO every day, from JioHotstar’s films and shows to a new Nepali film every week and live international sport. We are bringing that choice together on a platform built for Nepal, at pricing designed for our viewers.”

The Nepal launch follows JioHotstar’s expansion into the UK, Canada, Singapore and MENA, as the streaming platform builds its presence across international markets through direct launches and partnerships.

publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Nepal posted 280 against hosts Oman in their final ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup League 2 match on Monday, with Rohit Paudel and Dipendra Singh Airee rescuing the innings with a record 139-run stand for the fourth wicket.

After winning the toss at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground, Nepal were bowled out for 280 in 50 overs. They got off to a poor start, with opener Aasif Sheikh dismissed for seven.

Dev Khanal and Ishan Pandey added 64 runs for the second wicket. Pandey scored 29 off 60 balls before departing, while Khanal made 57 off 65 balls, including four fours and a six, for his fourth ODI half-century.

Khanal was playing his first match of the ongoing tri-series, having replaced Arjun Kumal.

Paudel and Airee steadied the innings with a 139-run partnership for the fourth wicket, Nepal’s highest for that wicket in ODI cricket. Airee scored 69 off 62 balls, hitting four sixes and three fours, while Paudel top-scored with 80 off 81 balls, including two fours and two sixes.

With that innings, Paudel became the first and only Nepali batter to reach 1,000 runs in the current cycle of the League 2 competition.

Bashir Ahmed provided a late boost, scoring 17 off just seven balls to help Nepal finish with a challenging total.

title: Nepal to prioritize climate justice, adaptation and loss and damage at COP-31 - The Rising Nepal
description: Nepal to prioritize climate justice, adaptation and loss and damage at COP-31  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Oct 19: Nepal is preparing to prioritize climate justice, protection of the Himalayan region, climate adaptation, and climate-related loss and damage at the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP-31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

COP-31 is scheduled to take place in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20.

The Ministry of Forests and Environment said Nepal would draw the international community's attention to the risks and damages the country has suffered from climate change despite its negligible contribution to global greenhouse gas emissions.

Ministry Secretary Rajendra Prasad Mishra said climate change was increasing risks in the Himalayan region, with recent disasters highlighting the vulnerability of mountain communities.

He said Nepal was focusing on protecting the Himalayan region and drawing international attention to the losses suffered by vulnerable communities. Preparations were also underway to make Nepal's delegation to COP-31 organized, effective and inclusive, he added.

"We want the delegation to be organized, effective and inclusive. Discussions are underway to form an effective delegation with representatives from all concerned ministries and civil society," Secretary Mishra said.

Nepal will participate in COP-31 under the leadership of Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal. Forests and Environment Minister Gita Chaudhary will also attend the conference.

Nepal has consistently highlighted the climate-related risks facing the Himalayan region at international climate conferences. Secretary Mishra said recent disasters had further underscored the region's vulnerability and the need for greater international attention.

"Since the beginning, we have been raising the issue that the Himalayan region is at high risk from climate change. Recent disasters have reinforced the need to view the region from a different perspective. Our efforts are focused on linking the risks facing the Himalayan region, climate adaptation, loss and damage, and climate justice with an effective implementation mechanism," he said.

As part of preparations for COP-31, the government plans to organize a national conference on October 29, bringing together representatives of sectoral ministries, foreign diplomatic missions in Nepal, development partners, civil society and the private sector.

Joint Secretary Dr Maheshwar Dhakal, chief of the ministry's Climate Change Management Division, said Nepal's national position paper and policy documents on climate change would be released at the conference.

According to him, the position paper will be finalized after incorporating suggestions from participants and feedback from the international community. It will cover the protection of the Himalayan region, climate adaptation, reduction of carbon emissions and the potential impacts of rising global temperatures on the mountains.

"Disasters in the Bhotekoshi and Budhigandaki river systems have heightened awareness of climate change impacts and climate-related disaster risks in the Himalayan region. Earlier disasters in Melamchi, Thame, Manang, Mustang, Kanchanpur and Ilam have also highlighted the challenges posed by climate change," Dhakal said.

The ministry is also preparing to involve civil society, the private sector and the media, alongside government representatives, to highlight Nepal's climate risks and conservation efforts before the international community.

Nepal will set up a pavilion at the conference venue in a space provided by the Turkish government. According to Dhakal, the pavilion will host discussions and showcase photographs and videos highlighting disasters in flood-prone areas, the vulnerability of the Himalayan region, climate change impacts and the challenges facing Nepal.

The ministry is seeking financial support and collaboration from development partners and non-governmental organizations to establish the pavilion.

Nepal has been raising climate justice at international forums

Nepal has been advocating climate justice at various international forums, including through the group of least developed countries, the United Nations and successive COP conferences.

The ministry said the commitment to climate justice expressed by Prime Minister Balendra Shah at the United Nations General Assembly and the issues raised by Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal at the pre-COP meeting would also inform Nepal's priorities at COP-31.

Joint Secretary Dhakal said discussions were underway at the international level to facilitate Nepal's access to the Fund for responding to Loss and Damage to support relief and rehabilitation following climate-related disasters.

He expressed hope that an announcement on assistance from the fund, based on Nepal's submissions, would be made by COP-31.

Climate scientist Kushal Gurung said Nepal needed to expand access to international climate finance and make carbon trading more effective to address climate change impacts and recover from disaster-related losses.

He said mobilizing climate finance, addressing loss and damage, and promoting carbon trading should be among Nepal's key priorities.

Gurung identified mobilizing the resources required to implement Nepal's third nationally determined contribution (NDC 3.0) as a major challenge. He said Nepal should prioritize grants and concessional financing when expanding access to climate finance to avoid increasing its debt burden and creating additional economic risks.

He also stressed the need for Nepal to present evidence-based scientific assessments of recent disasters in the Bhotekoshi and other areas at COP-31 to garner international support for addressing the resulting losses and damages.

"Securing sufficient assistance from disaster relief funds for post-disaster relief and recovery is challenging. Nepal should therefore also advocate for a financial mechanism that can be activated immediately during disasters and a fund that can provide assistance promptly," he said.

Gurung said Nepal should strengthen bilateral cooperation with other countries to expand carbon trading, which he described as an important avenue for mobilizing climate finance.

He added that providing international partners with clear information on Nepal's carbon trading potential, investment opportunities, project locations and necessary legal provisions could help attract greater investment and cooperation in the sector.(RSS)
